newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-WOOSNAM SHARES LEAD AFTER 68 BUT THEN COMPLAINS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM SHARES LEAD AFTER 68 BUT THEN COMPLAINS.

text.p: Ian Woosnam grabbed a share of the early second round lead in the Lancome Trophy on Friday, then said Colin Montgomerie, his rival for the European Order of Merit, was getting preferential treatment at tournaments.

Woosnam, who trails Montgomerie by 60,000 pounds ($94,000) in the title race, shot a two-under-par 68 to join first round leader Jamie Spence on five under par, with Spence and Montgomerie among the late starters on Friday.

The Welshman suggested Montgomerie, who shot an opening 66, was gaining an advantage by being allowed to play early in the first round of several events, while he played late on the first day and early on the second.

"He gets the first punch in," Woosnam said. "If he makes a good score, I have to try to match it and that puts me under "It seems to have happened several times. I don't know if it is done by the draw or if he asks it to be that way," he added, saying he felt Montgomerie had been given several more first round starts than he had.
World number two Nick Faldo managed only a one-over 71 and on four over par with 145 faced an anxious wait of several hours to be sure he had made the halfway cut for the final two rounds.
The U.S. Masters champion was expected to be safe but with half the field still to start their second rounds, it was far from certain.
Faldo, who began with a 73, said he was "playing so badly" and blamed his hip action for his troubles.
"I'm having trouble moving my hips. I've been working so hard at it my left hip is now sore.
"When I came here I was struggling. My hips are my Achilles heel, my Achilles hip, if you like," he joked.
"But at least I'm still here to keep grinding. Maybe I'll find something," he added, confident he would escape the cut.
A birdie at the 13th, his fourth, signalled a slight return to form but it was his only one and he bogeyed the third and sixth holes on his second nine.
Woosnam also began at the 10th and had birdie twos at the 12th and 18th holes on putts of 12 and 25 feet.
He birdied the second from 10 feet, saved par three times from off the green but bogeyed the last when his drive finished behind a tree.
Woosnam said he still had a stiff back and for the second day in succession he required physiotherapy.
He said he is suffering from spondylosis, a deterioration of two vertebrae in his back.
Woosnam's partner in the 1993 Ryder Cup, Englishman Peter Baker, moved up to challenge with a 69 to stand on four under par, one off the lead.
He said his play for two rounds was down to better putting, which he achieved "by standing taller to the ball."
German Bernhard Langer, who led for a time on Thursday at five under before completing a 67, added a second round 71 as the early magic from his broomhandled putter seemed to vanish.
